question: Every section of a current-carrying circular wire contributes to the magnetic field at the centre of the loop in ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**the same direction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When a current flows through a **circular wire**, it creates a **magnetic field** around it due to the motion of electric charges. This behavior is explained by **Ampere's Circuital Law** and **Biot-Savart Law**.
 
• Every small segment of the circular loop contributes to the **magnetic field at the center of the loop** in the **same direction**. This is due to the **symmetry** of the circular loop and the nature of the magnetic field lines.
 
• The **direction of the magnetic field** at the center of the loop is determined using the **Right-Hand Thumb Rule**: If the thumb of the right hand points in the direction of the current, the curled fingers around the loop indicate the direction of the magnetic field.
 
• The magnetic field created by each segment of the wire at the center of the loop **adds up** constructively because all the contributions are in the **same direction**.
